What it does Terminal UI Vim-style keys, three panes, an inline field editor. Run kru with no arguments. Scriptable CLI Every command has --json , stable ids and predictable exit codes. Private buckets Encrypt a bucket with a password (Argon2id + XChaCha20-Poly1305). Git sync Keep devices in step through any private git repo, with automatic merging. Rich tasks Priority, status, natural due dates ( fri , 3d ), context and markdown notes. Agent friendly Ships a SKILL.md so LLM agents can drive it safely. The model in 30 seconds A task has a description, priority, status, optional due date, free-form context and an optional markdown notes file. Every task lives in a bucket (e.g. work , home ). One bucket is active ; task add uses it by default. Tasks are shown ordered by urgency: open before done, then earliest due date, then priority. Done tasks are cleaned up automatically after 7 days. Data is plain JSON files in one directory, so it is easy to back up or sync. The name kru comes from the Sanskrit root कृ ( kṛ ), “to do”, the root of karma (action) and kartavya (what is to be done), which is what a todo list holds. Next: install kru , then take the five minute tour .

Install kru is a single static binary. Pick whichever route suits you. Prebuilt binaries Download the archive for your system from the latest release . System Archive macOS, Apple silicon kru-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz macOS, Intel kru-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz Linux, x86_64 kru-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz Linux, ARM64 kru-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz Windows, x86_64 kru-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip The Linux binaries are static and run on any distribution. Each archive has a .sha256 file beside it to verify the download. macOS and Linux target=aarch64-apple-darwin # pick from the table above mkdir -p ~/.local/bin curl -fsSL "https://github.com/SuhrudhSarathy/kru/releases/latest/download/kru-$target.tar.gz" \ | tar xz -C ~/.local/bin kru Make sure ~/.local/bin is on your PATH . If a browser-downloaded binary is blocked on macOS, clear the quarantine flag: xattr -d com.apple.quarantine ~/.local/bin/kru . Windows Unzip kru-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip and put kru.exe in a folder on your PATH . From source With Rust 1.89 or newer: cargo install --git https://github.com/SuhrudhSarathy/kru --locked Shell completion Tab completes commands and flags, plus your bucket names, task numbers and setting names (e.g. kru task list -b <Tab> ). Add the line for your shell to its startup file: source <(COMPLETE=zsh kru) # ~/.zshrc source <(COMPLETE=bash kru) # ~/.bashrc COMPLETE=fish kru | source # ~/.config/fish/config.fish Check it works $ kru --version

Getting started A five minute tour of the everyday commands. 1. Create a bucket Tasks live in buckets, so make one first. The first bucket you create becomes the active one. $ kru bucket add work $ kru bucket add home $ kru bucket list 2. Add tasks $ kru task add -d "Write quarterly report" -p high --due fri $ kru task add -d "Pay rent" -b home --due 3d -c "Landlord: Sam" Without -b , the active bucket is used. Change it with kru bucket use home . See Tasks & fields for every flag and the due-date formats. 3. Look at them $ kru task list # open tasks, most urgent first $ kru task list -b home -p high # filter $ kru task list -q report # search descriptions $ kru task list --all # include done tasks $ kru task show 1 # every detail of task #1 4. Change and finish them $ kru task mark 1 -s in-progress -p medium $ kru task ctx 1 -a "Draft shared with Priya" # append a note line $ kru task md 1 # open a markdown notes file in your editor $ kru task move 1 -b home $ kru task done 1 2 Numbers shift, ids don't. Tasks are numbered bucket by bucket, so adding or removing a task can change other tasks' numbers. Anything that takes a task also accepts its id (or the start of it). Prefer ids in scripts. 5. Use the terminal UI $ kru Press a to add, space to toggle done, x to expand a task, q to quit. Full key list in Terminal UI . 6. Keep devices in step (optional) Create an empty private git repository (e.g. on GitHub), then on each device: $ kru sync init git@github.com:you/my-tasks.git Details in Syncing . Requires git .

Terminal UI Run kru with no command to open it. The screen has three panes: Buckets , Tasks (open tasks of the selected bucket) and Done (finished tasks). The footer always shows the keys available right now, and the latest message (green) or error (red). Tasks & fields What a task holds and how to set it. Fields Field Flag Values description -d , --description One line of text, required, up to 500 characters ctx -c , --ctx Extra context; may span lines; up to 10,000 characters priority -p , --priority low , medium , high (also l , m / med , h ) status -s , --status todo , in-progress , done (also doing , wip ) due --due See below; none clears it Kru also records created , edited and completed times, a stable id , and an optional notes file. Values are case-insensitive. Input is tidied: control characters are dropped and runs of spaces collapse. Due dates All parsed in your local time zone. A date without a time means the end of that day . You type Meaning today , tomorrow End of that day mon … sunday End of the next such weekday 2026-10-12 End of that date "2026-10-12 17:00" That exact time 3d , +2h , 1w , 2 days Now plus that span none , clear , - No due date Ordering Lists are ordered most urgent first: open before done, then earliest due date (no due date last), then higher priority. Identifying a task Commands take a <task> argument. It can be: its number (digits only), as shown in task list . Numbers run bucket by bucket and can shift. its id (UUID), or a unique start of it. Ids never change, even across devices. Context vs. markdown notes Context is a short text field on the task. Append with kru task ctx 1 -a "text" ; replacing it asks for confirmation (or needs --force ). Markdown notes are for anything longer: kru task md 1 creates notes/<id>.md in your store (starting with the description as a heading) and opens it in your editor. --path prints the path instead, --remove deletes the file. Removing or pruning the task removes its notes too. Notes sync as text. Done tasks and pruning Tasks done more than 7 days ago are deleted whenever kru starts. Run it yourself with kru prune --days N .

Buckets A bucket is a named list of tasks: a project, a context, an area of life. kru bucket add work # create; the first one becomes active kru bucket list # * marks the active bucket kru bucket use home # default for `kru task add` kru bucket rename work job kru bucket remove job # asks first if it has open tasks; --force skips Names are matched case-insensitively. task add fails if the bucket doesn't exist, or if none is given and none is active. Removing a bucket with open tasks needs --force and deletes those tasks. Merging devices (see Syncing ) combines buckets that share a name. A bucket can be made private : encrypted and hidden. Move a task between buckets with kru task move <task> -b <bucket> , or m in the TUI.

CLI reference Every command. kru <command> --help is always the authority. Global options Flag Meaning --json Print JSON instead of text. Works anywhere on the command line. --unlock Ask for the password of private buckets and show them for this command -h , --help Help -V , --version Version kru with no command opens the TUI (with --json it is an error instead). kru task Command What it does task add Add a task. -d required; -b bucket (default: active); plus -c -p -s --due task list (ls) List tasks. Filters: -b bucket, -s status, -p priority, -q text, -a include done task show <task> Every detail of a task task mark <task> (edit) Change fields with -d -c -p -s --due . All-or-nothing; setting an unchanged value is a no-op task ctx <task> [text] Show context; -a text appends a line; text replaces (asks unless -f ) task md <task> Open the markdown notes in your editor (creating them). --path prints the path; --remove deletes (asks unless -f ) task done <task>… Mark one or more tasks done task move <task> -b <bucket> (mv) Move to another bucket task remove <task>… (rm) Remove tasks kru bucket Command What it does bucket add <name> [--private] Create a bucket (optionally encrypted) bucket private <name> Make an existing bucket private bucket list (ls) List buckets; * marks the active one bucket use <name> Make it the default for task add bucket rename <name> <new> Rename bucket remove <name> [--force] (rm) Remove a bucket and its tasks kru sync Command What it does sync Commit, fetch, merge and push sync init <remote> Set up syncing with a git remote, then sync sync status Where syncing stands, without touching the network kru config Command What it does config / config list Every setting, its value and its source config get <key> One setting config set <key> <value> Change a setting config unset <key> Fall back to env or default config path The config file's path Other Command What it does prune [--days N] Delete done tasks completed more than N days ago (default 7) path Print where kru stores its data Exit codes Code Meaning 0 Success; JSON (with --json ) on stdout 1 Failure; nothing on stdout; stderr is one line starting Error: 2 Bad arguments; stderr starts error:

Private buckets Encrypt a bucket with a password. Locked, it doesn't exist as far as kru is concerned. Using them kru bucket add diary --private # new, encrypted bucket (asks for a password) kru bucket private home # encrypt an existing bucket kru task list --unlock # show private buckets for this command In the TUI, P unlocks and L locks again. Locked private buckets are hidden from every command: lists, JSON output and task numbering. Their names are hidden too. The password is typed on the terminal and can't be passed any other way, so scripts and agents can't read or change private buckets. task add without -b fails if the active bucket is private and locked. Notes of tasks in a private bucket are encrypted inside the bucket rather than kept as a plain file. They open only in your editor ( task md --path is refused). Making a bucket private moves its notes inside and deletes the plain files. A forgotten password can't be recovered. Without it the tasks cannot be decrypted. There is no reset. How it's encrypted Key derivation: Argon2id (19 MiB, 2 passes by default) with a random 16-byte salt per bucket. Cipher: XChaCha20-Poly1305, with a fresh random nonce every time the bucket is sealed. What's encrypted: the bucket's name, tasks and notes, as JSON. The bucket id is used as associated data, so a sealed bucket can't be passed off as another. What stays readable: only the header (id and timestamps), so sync can tell which version is newer without the password. Private buckets sync like any other: the git remote only ever sees the encrypted form.

Syncing Keep tasks in step across devices using any git remote. Set up Create an empty private repository (for example on GitHub). On each device, with the same URL: kru sync init git@github.com:you/my-tasks.git This turns the store directory into a git repository with an origin remote, writes a .gitignore for device-local files ( state.json , locks), and runs a first sync. Requires git on your PATH . kru never prompts for credentials with --json ; a remote that needs a password fails instead of waiting. Everyday use kru sync # commit local changes, fetch, merge, push kru sync status # remote, last sync, local changes, ahead/behind (no network) In the TUI press S . Turn on autosync ( kru config set autosync on ) to sync in the background after every change and every five minutes in the TUI. Output goes to sync.log in the store. How merging works Git moves the data and keeps history; kru does the merging. Every task and bucket has a stable uuid, so when two devices both changed things, kru does a three-way merge per task and bucket against their common ancestor: A change made on one device is taken. If the same field changed on both, the later edit wins . An edit made after a delete elsewhere keeps the task; a delete made after an edit removes it. Buckets with the same name are merged. Markdown notes merge as text. If both devices changed the same lines, the more recently committed file wins. Each decision is reported, e.g. priority: kept high over low . Nothing is silently lost: git history keeps every version. Task numbers differ between devices and can shift after a sync. Ids are the same everywhere. Privacy Private buckets are encrypted before they are committed, so even your remote host only sees ciphertext for them. Other buckets are stored as readable JSON, which is why the repository should be private.

Settings & storage Where data lives kru path prints the store directory. The first match wins: $KRU_DIR the dir setting your platform's cache folder Inside are plain JSON files for buckets and tasks, plus notes/<id>.md for markdown notes. Files carry a format version: an older kru refuses to touch data written by a newer one, so upgrade rather than hand-editing. Several kru processes (say a CLI call and an open TUI) can share a store safely: saves lock the store and merge what another process saved meanwhile. For a throwaway store (tests, dry runs): export KRU_DIR="$(mktemp -d)" . Settings Stored in a JSON file in your config folder ( kru config path ; e.g. ~/.config/kru/config.json on Linux). $KRU_CONFIG points elsewhere. Key Meaning Effective value dir Where tasks are stored $KRU_DIR , else setting, else cache folder editor Command to open files, e.g. nvim , code --wait setting, else $VISUAL , $EDITOR , then vi ( notepad on Windows) autosync on / off : sync in the background setting, else off kru config # everything, with where each value came from kru config set editor "code --wait" kru config set autosync on kru config unset editor Changing dir doesn't move existing data. Environment variables Variable Purpose KRU_DIR Override the store directory KRU_CONFIG Override the config file path VISUAL , EDITOR Fallback editor COMPLETE Generate shell completions ( see Install )

Scripts & agents kru's JSON output is its stable interface. The repo ships a SKILL.md that teaches LLM agents to use it. Ground rules Always pass --json . Text output may change. Never run bare kru from a script: it opens the interactive TUI. Check the exit code. Non-zero means failure with a one-line message on stderr. Refer to tasks by id , not number. Use --all to see done tasks. Append context ( task ctx -a ) instead of overwriting; replacing needs --force . Task JSON { "num": 1, "bucket": "home", "description": "Pay rent", "ctx": "Landlord: Sam", "priority": "high", "status": "todo", "due": "2026-10-12T11:30:00Z", "completed": null, "created": "2026-10-10T12:49:45Z", "edited": "2026-10-10T12:49:45Z", "mdpath": "notes/01a125dc-….md", "id": "01a125dc-bcef-7784-8fc5-17784df85dec" } Times are RFC 3339 UTC, so they compare correctly as strings. New keys may appear in future versions; ignore ones you don't know. Recipes # add and remember the id id=$(kru task add -d "Write report" -p high --due fri -b work --json | jq -r .id) # change fields and see what changed kru task mark "$id" -s in-progress --json | jq .changes # overdue tasks now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) kru task list --json | jq --arg n "$now" '[.[] | select(.due != null and .due < $n)]' # complete them all kru task list --json | jq -r --arg n "$now" '.[] | select(.due != null and .due < $n) | .id' \ | xargs -r kru task done --json # open tasks per bucket kru bucket list --json | jq 'map({(.name): .open}) | add' Private buckets and agents Agents cannot see or change private buckets : the password can only be typed at a terminal. If a task can't be found, it may be in one; ask the user to run the command with --unlock . Using the skill with Claude Code Copy SKILL.md into a .claude/skills/kru/ directory (project) or ~/.claude/skills/kru/ (personal) and the agent will use kru for task requests. The file also documents the complete error table.

Workflows Recipes that combine the pieces. Each is self-contained. A daily routine with the TUI Open kru . Tasks are already ordered most urgent first, so the top of Tasks is what to do next. Press s on what you start ( in-progress ), space when it's done. Capture new work with a ; set the due date with d ( fri , 3d , tomorrow ). Put long-running detail in notes with o rather than in the description. Finished tasks sit in Done for a week, then vanish. Reopen one with space . Syncing a laptop and a desktop # once: make an EMPTY PRIVATE repo, e.g. github.com/you/my-tasks laptop$ kru sync init git@github.com:you/my-tasks.git desktop$ kru sync init git@github.com:you/my-tasks.git # same URL # from now on kru config set autosync on # background sync after changes If both edit the same task before syncing, kru merges field by field, and the later edit wins for a field both touched. See Syncing . Quick capture from the shell alias t='kru task add -d' t "Call the dentist" --due tomorrow -p medium Show what's due in your prompt or status bar # count of open tasks due within a day kru task list --json | jq --arg c "$(date -u -d '+1 day' +%FT%TZ)" \ '[.[] | select(.due != null and .due <= $c)] | length' On macOS replace date -u -d '+1 day' with date -u -v+1d . A morning reminder with cron # crontab -e : weekdays at 9, print overdue/today tasks (mail or notify-send as you like) 0 9 * * 1-5 kru task list --json | jq -r '.[] | select(.due != null) | "\(.due[:10]) \(.description)"' | sort | head Moving a project to its own bucket kru bucket add launch kru task list -q "launch" --json | jq -r '.[].id' | xargs -I{} kru task move {} -b launch Keeping sensitive tasks private kru bucket add finance --private kru task add -b finance -d "File taxes" --unlock See Private buckets .

How it works The design behind kru, for the curious and for contributors. On-disk layout <store dir>/ ├── state.json # active bucket; device-local, not synced ├── buckets/ │ └── <bucket id>.json # one file per bucket, with its tasks ├── notes/ │ └── <task id>.md # markdown notes (plain buckets only) ├── tombstones.json # what was deleted, and when (for sync) ├── .lock # held while saving └── .git/, .gitignore, sync.log # only once sync is set up Find the directory with kru path . Everything is readable JSON (except private buckets, which are sealed), so you can back it up with any tool. Identity: ids vs numbers Every task and bucket has a UUID that never changes. The number you see ( #3 ) is just its position in the display order, computed on the fly, which is why numbers shift. Sync, notes and scripts all key on ids. Format versioning Every file records its format version and the kru release that wrote it. When a file is read it is upgraded step by step in memory and written back in the current format on the next save. A file from a newer kru is refused instead of misread, so upgrade kru rather than editing data by hand. Concurrent access Saves take a lock on the store, re-read what's on disk and merge in whatever another process saved meanwhile. A CLI call never undoes what an open TUI did, or the other way round. Retention Done tasks are pruned when kru starts, after 7 days. Tombstones (records of deletions) are kept 90 days. A device that hasn't synced for longer may bring a task that was deleted elsewhere back. Why git for sync Git already gives transport, authentication, history and hosting for free, and kru's data is small text files. kru adds the part git can't do for this data: a structured, id-based three-way merge, so two devices editing different fields of one task never produce a conflict marker. See Syncing . Code map Path Responsibility src/store/ The store: loading, saving, locking, migrations, notes, tombstones, private buckets src/task.rs , src/bucket.rs The data types and their fields src/privacy.rs Key derivation and sealing of private buckets src/sync/ Git wrapper, snapshots and the three-way merge src/cli/ Commands, argument parsing, text and JSON output, completion src/tui/ Event mapping, app state and rendering (ratatui) The CLI and TUI both go through the same Store methods, so they behave identically.

Rust library The kru crate is also a library, the same one the CLI and TUI are built on. The API is young and may change between releases. Pin a version or a git revision. Depend on it [dependencies] kru = { git = "https://github.com/SuhrudhSarathy/kru" } Modules Module What's in it kru::task Task , Priority , Status kru::bucket Bucket : add, get, search, filter tasks kru::store Store : the persistent store ( Store::open , save , buckets, notes, private buckets) kru::sync Syncing and the merge kru::config Settings kru::privacy Sealing and unsealing buckets Example use jiff::{Timestamp, ToSpan}; use kru::bucket::Bucket; use kru::task::{Priority, Status, Task}; let mut home = Bucket::new("Home"); let id = home.add( Task::new("Buy groceries") .with_priority(Priority::High) .with_due(Timestamp::now() + 24.hours()), ); home.get_mut(id).unwrap().set_status(Status::InProgress); for task in home.search("groceries") { println!("{}", task.description); } A longer, runnable version lives in examples/api.rs : cargo run --example api . Build the API reference locally with cargo doc --open .

FAQ & troubleshooting My tasks disappeared Private bucket? Locked private buckets are completely hidden. Run the command with --unlock , or press P in the TUI. Different store? kru path shows which directory is in use. A leftover KRU_DIR in your shell, or a changed dir setting, points kru somewhere else. kru config shows where each value comes from. Done tasks? task list hides them. Add --all . They're deleted after 7 days. A task's number changed Numbers are positions, recomputed bucket by bucket. Use the task's id (or the start of it) whenever you need something stable. kru task show 3 --json | jq -r .id gets it. no bucket given and no active bucket set Create one ( kru bucket add work ) or pick one ( kru bucket use work ), or pass -b . macOS refuses to run the downloaded binary xattr -d com.apple.quarantine ~/.local/bin/kru kru: command not found Add the install folder to your PATH , e.g. export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" in your shell's startup file. Sync problems Message Fix git isn't installed Install git and make sure it's on your PATH sync isn't set up for this store Run kru sync init <remote-url> first this store already syncs with <url> sync init was given a different remote than the one already configured git fetch failed / git push failed Network or access problem. Nothing is lost; check your SSH key or token and retry A background sync (autosync) logs to sync.log in the store directory. I forgot my private bucket's password It can't be recovered: the tasks are encrypted with a key derived from it, and there is no backdoor. Remove the bucket and start again. "written by a newer kru" Another device (or a newer install) saved the data in a newer format. Upgrade kru on this device. Don't edit the files by hand. The TUI won't take Alt+Enter for a new line Some terminals send Enter and Alt+Enter as the same key. Use Ctrl+J , which works everywhere. The editor that opens isn't the one I want kru config set editor "code --wait" Where do I report a bug? GitHub issues . Include kru --version and your OS.
